filtersOrSort: Client-side only: mobile FILTERS pills (all/video/course/audio/pdf/template/image) filter the already-fetched `items` array in-memory by `contentType` via useMemo — no filter/sort query params are ever sent to the API. No sort control exists; list order is whatever the response returns (mock data is reverse-chronological by purchasedAt, not explicitly re-sorted client-side).
reads.pagination: None. GET /api/hub/content/purchases returns the full purchases array in one response (PurchasesResponse.items); no page/cursor param, no infinite scroll, no 'load more' — matches conventions.md's offset-pagination default but this screen's mock/seam never exercises it.

uiStatesHandled.state: loading (initial fetch, mobile skeleton rows + desktop skeleton grid)
uiStatesHandled.entersWhen: items === null (before getPurchases() resolves, on mount or after a retry from load())
getPurchases() promise rejects, caught by the page's own .catch(() => setError(...))
uiStatesHandled.reachable: no — src/lib/api/purchases.ts wraps apiFetch in its own try/catch and falls back to mockPurchases (a resolved success) on any failure, so the page-level .catch never fires while the mock fallback exists; in mock mode (USE_MOCKS=true, the current default) apiFetch throws a MockModeError immediately and is swallowed internally before it ever reaches the page. Even once a real backend is wired, this try-fetch-then-mock-fallback pattern means a real backend outage would still silently resolve to stale mock data instead of surfacing this error state, unless the mock fallback is stripped.

gapNotes: The desktop design's 'Also bought' panel includes a WAWUBasket order row, but the shipped code's AlsoTracked component deliberately omits WAWUBasket/WAWUBeauty items — the code's own comment states 'those are handoff-only external apps (CLAUDE.md) with no order-tracking data model here.' This is a genuine designed-vs-handled gap, not a mock/backend gap: no order-tracking entity for external marketplace purchases exists anywhere in this screen's data layer, and per CLAUDE.md's WAWUBasket/WAWUBeauty handoff-only rule, building one would likely be out of scope rather than a missing backend contract.

No loading, empty, or error frame exists in either design source for this screen — both frames only depict the fully-populated success state; loading/empty/error handling in the shipped code has no design-source backing to verify against, it is purely a code-level UI-states convention (per conventions.md's 'required UI states: loading/empty/error-with-retry/success on every data surface').
